newsitem.title: POLAND: ADVISER FOR LOT SALE SEEN BY END APRIL 97.
newsitem.headline: ADVISER FOR LOT SALE SEEN BY END APRIL 97.

text.p: Poland's Transport Ministry believes an adviser for the partial sell-off of the national air carrier PLL LOT will be picked by the end of April next year, a ministry official said on Tuesday.

Ryszard Zaremba, head of the civil air department told a news conference that in January the ministry planned to re-start negotiations with the six consortia shortlisted in the tender annulled earlier this year.

But he said the final decision to invite the consortia to talks and the choice of adviser would depend on the treasury ministry, which would take over the formal ownership of LOT from January 1, 1997.
"We would like to invite firms for negotiations in January next year ... if this is done we could expect closing them by the end of April," he said.
In June the transport minister annulled the tender for an adviser in the LOT privatisation because he felt the fees bidders' asked for were too high.
The bidders shortlisted in the tender include the following consortia:
- McKinsey and Company, Barclays de Zoete Wedd Ltd, Arthur Andersen, Hutton and Williams as well as BRE bank
- SBC Warburg and Polish units of Clifford Chance and Price Waterhouse
- Merrill Lynch International Ltd, the Warsaw-based bank Pekao SA and the Polish unit of White and Case
- West Merchant Bank Ltd and Lufthansa Consulting GmbH.
Two Western investment banks, Salomon Brothers International
Ltd and Dresdner Bank's Kleinwort Benson Ltd, made individual
Zaremba also said the ministry believed LOT had to be privatised in 1997 or 1998 to make the sale largely profitable.
